record_title: Prime-square local rigidity for 31 unresolved exponents in the Lebesgue-Nagell equation
scientific_context: For 31 of the 84 unresolved prime exponents 17 <= p <= 911 in x^2-2=y^p, the Katz-Pratt Thue equation has only the trivial residue class compatible modulo p^2. Consequently every integer solution satisfies y == -1 (mod p) and x == +/-1 (mod p^2), proving the Katz-Pratt local-triviality conjecture for those exponents.
limitations: This is a partial local result and does not exclude nontrivial global integer solutions. For the other 53 residual prime exponents, multiple residue classes survive the p^2 test. Originality is to the best of our knowledge; the most directly relevant Katz-Pratt source was revised in September 2026, so residual bibliographic risk from very recent work remains. The finite enumeration is computer-assisted but exact and reproducible; no formal proof-assistant verification or independent audit is asserted.

artifact_inventory.description: Standalone exact verification of the prime-square residue criterion for all 84 residual exponents using two exact arithmetic evaluations.
Deterministic output listing the 31 unique-branch primes and branch counts for all 84 residual exponents.
